title: Stoughton town manager contradicts police chief who accused him of tampering with Sandra Birchmore investigation
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Town Manager Thomas Calter denies interfering with investigations on Sandra Birchmore, countering claims by Police Chief Donna McNamara.
Calter refutes McNamara's lawsuit alleging harassment and discriminatory actions, stating he has not pressured her into resigning.
Calter addresses unions' no-confidence vote, asserting pride in his tenure and commitment to investigation integrity.

title: Nearly 30 people arrested after investigation into drug trafficking in Western Mass.
author: Audrey Cooney
bullets: Twenty-eight individuals were arrested in a Western Massachusetts drug trafficking probe led by the FBI’s Western Massachusetts Gang Task Force.
Law enforcement seized over 12 firearms and more than one kilogram of cocaine, along with fentanyl and heroin.
Operation Pinky Promise targeted drug activities in Chicopee, Holyoke, and Springfield using surveillance, confidential sources, and wiretaps.

title: Patriots stock watch 2.0: Who’s rising and falling ahead of preseason opener?
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Romeo Doubs, Drake Maye, and Will Campbell are among the Patriots players showing improvement ahead of preseason.
Tommy DeVito and DeMario Douglas impressed during joint practices, strengthening their case for playing time in the upcoming games.
Reserve cornerbacks struggled without starters, while Behren Morton and Jam Miller face uncertain roster situations due to competition.

title: Public art tiles stolen out of sidewalk in Dedham, town says
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Four art tiles were stolen from a new public pathway at Sawmill Park Pollinator Pathway in Dedham.
The tiles, part of a 40-tile Biodiversity Art Walk, were funded by the Massachusetts Community Biodiversity Grant Program.
Dedham Police will monitor the area to prevent further thefts; the ribbon cutting will proceed as planned on August 19.

title: The best waterfront hotel in America is in Massachusetts, according to USA Today readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Chatham Bars Inn in Chatham, Massachusetts, ranked as the best waterfront hotel in America by USA Today readers in 2026.
Chatham Bars Inn features a quarter-mile private beach, ocean views, 25 acres of landscaping, and multiple dining options.
Madison Beach Hotel in Madison, Connecticut, also ranked high, securing the No. 4 spot on USA Today's list.

title: Are millionaires really leaving Massachusetts? We don’t know yet.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IRS data on high-income migration post-2023 millionaires tax in Massachusetts is still unavailable, fueling ongoing debate.
Massachusetts lost over 30,000 residents to other states by mid-2025, but income levels of these movers remain unclear.
The millionaires tax has raised substantial revenue, but whether it triggered wealthy residents to leave is uncertain.

title: 7 things to do during a rainy day on the Cape
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Visit the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy's Shark Center in Chatham for interactive exhibits and a fossil digging experience.
Explore museums like the John F. Kennedy Hyannis Museum and the Wydah Pirate Museum on a rainy Cape day.
Attend a show at the Cape Playhouse in Dennis or watch a movie at the historic Chatham Orpheum Theater.

title: Visit to Boston made Boca Raton resident feel miserable about living in Boca Raton
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Ian Pinto from Boca Raton shared his admiration for Boston after a recent four-day visit.
Pinto noted Boston's walkability, affordable dining, and favorable public transportation compared to Boca Raton.
Pinto appreciated Boston's welcoming atmosphere and plans to visit more cities inspired by his experience.

title: Motorcyclist killed in crash with pickup truck in Raynham
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 31-year-old motorcyclist was killed in a crash with a pickup truck at Route 138 and Elm Street in Raynham.
The victim, Jason Marshall from Taunton, was transported to a hospital where he was pronounced dead.
The driver of the Chevy Silverado, a 57-year-old man, stayed on scene and spoke with police; investigation ongoing.

title: N.H. police seek to identify suspects who fatally shot dog in attempted armed robbery
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A dog was fatally shot during an attempted armed robbery in Hollis, New Hampshire early Tuesday morning.
Police report a man and a woman displayed a firearm and demanded money from the victim on Laurel Hill Road.
Authorities request residents with security cameras check footage from 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. for suspect identification.
